* **Member Name:** Jordan Foster

* **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)
* **Provider:** Reyes, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
* **Date of Notice:** 2026-08-07
* **Reference Number:** POC-EE22487639-86426

Dear Grievances and Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of coverage for my lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT code 63030), as requested by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Reyes. The denial letter dated August 7, 2026, states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. I am submitting this appeal to demonstrate that I have fully met—and indeed exceeded—the conservative treatment requirements mandated under your clinical guidelines.

### Applicable Medical Policy and Criteria

Your determination was made under the plan's medical policy managed by your specialty vendor, Evolent. Specifically, the governing policy is the **"Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery"** (effective July 1, 2026). 

According to this policy, surgical intervention is medically necessary when there is a:
> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"

The policy further clarifies how conservative treatment must be structured, stating:
> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

Under these guidelines:
* "Active Modalities" include "Physical therapy".
* "Inactive Modalities" include "Medications (e.g., NSAIDs, steroids, analgesics)" and "Injections (e.g., epidural steroid injection, selective nerve root block)".

Additionally, the guideline defines a failure of conservative treatment as a:
> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment"

### Patient Clinical History and Mapping to Criteria

My medical records demonstrate that I have participated in a comprehensive, multimodality non-operative treatment plan that satisfies every element of your criteria:

1. **Duration of Symptoms:** I have suffered from severe, progressive lower back pain and radiculopathy for 12 months, which has been completely unrelieved by rest.
2. **Active Component ("Physical therapy"):** I completed a highly structured, supervised physical therapy program that focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. This program spanned 10 weeks, from May 3, 2026, to July 12, 2026, and consisted of 16 completed visits. This conservative trial is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This 10-week trial vastly exceeds your "minimum of six (6) weeks" requirement and was completed entirely within the last six months.
3. **Inactive Component ("Medications (e.g., NSAIDs, steroids, analgesics)"):** I have consistently used prescribed NSAIDs for a period of 6 months, which have failed to provide adequate relief.
4. **Inactive Component ("Injections (e.g., epidural steroid injection, selective nerve root block)"):** To further manage my pain, I underwent a lumbar corticosteroid injection on June 9, 2026, which yielded only 3 weeks of partial relief before my pain returned to baseline.

Despite completing a full 10-week course of physical therapy alongside multiple inactive modalities, I experienced a "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment". 

### Diagnostic Findings and Functional Impairment

The clinical necessity of decompression is further supported by my imaging and physical examinations:
* **Imaging Correlation:** An MRI of my lumbar spine performed on June 28, 2026, confirms an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. 
* **Clinical Correlation:** My physical examination shows a positive provocative test on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding exactly to the compressed L5 nerve root.
* **Functional Deficit:** My symptoms severely hinder my daily activities. I experience debilitating radicular pain that radiates into my right calf, and my functional capacity has deteriorated to the point where I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes.
* **Additional Clinical Status:** I have no active infections, no untreated substance use disorders, am a non-smoker, and have a BMI of 29. 

### Conclusion

Because I have completed a documented 10-week trial of physical therapy (active modality) combined with a 6-month trial of NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection (inactive modalities) within the last six months without meaningful improvement, I have met all conservative care requirements under **"Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery"**.

I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for my decompression surgery so that I may proceed with Dr. Reyes's recommended treatment plan. 

If you require any additional information, please contact my provider, Dr. Reyes, at [Doctor's Phone Number] or contact me directly at the phone number listed above.

Sincerely,

Jordan Foster
